text:
Linus Karlsson's November has been louder than his stat line. The Canucks forward was the man on the ground when, per a House of Hockey headline, "Logan Cooley punches Canucks' Linus Karlsson while he's down," another scrum in a month Vancouver Hockey Daily summed up as "Another night ends in a scrum for the Canucks with Linus Karlsson drawing the attention."

The hockey underneath is steadier than the noise. He has 6 goals and 12 points in 27 games on 14:31 a night, and his 6.6 expected goals (the quality of his own chances) almost exactly match what he's scored. Both of his goals in the last ten games came in one night against Vegas, and the Canucks have won three of those ten.

Evolving-Hockey had him as a real play driver last season, 1.6 wins above replacement and 86th percentile for the chances his team created with him on, despite bottom-3% teammates. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking puts him in the home-plate area often (88th percentile). Our range has him on pace for about 19 goals. On a team losing this much, a third-round pick doing the dirty work is worth noticing.
headline: Karlsson is doing the hard part
